## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dibbasotakathā* (Kv 3.8) is a controversy located in the third chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994]. Within this section of the work, the text takes its place among debates regarding the powers and potentialities of a Tathāgata, emancipation, the faculties of the "eighth person" (*aṭṭhamaka puggala*), and the nature of the divine eye and divine ear (*dibbasota*) [Hazra 1994]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
No cross-language parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral or matched above threshold by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pāli literature, DharmaNexus records 105 matching passages across seven texts, reflecting the highly patterned dialectical structure of the *Kathāvatthu* [DharmaNexus]. The closest text-reuse partner is the immediately preceding chapter on the divine eye, the *Dibbacakkhukathā* (Kv 3.7), with 21 matches spanning 4,058 characters (longest §2.3–10.2 ↔ §2.4–10.2) [DharmaNexus]. Other recurring formulaic debate sequences are shared with *Adhigayhamanasikārakathā* (Kv 16.4), *Anāsavakathā* (Kv 4.3), *Nirodhakathā* (Kv 10.1), *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), *Ariyadhammavipākakathā* (Kv 7.9), and the commentary *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
